Collect 3 powerup crates in a single run. Only about 1 in 10 destroyed enemies
drops a crate and crates drift away, so keep destroying enemies and chase the
crates that appear. If your HEALTH empties before your third crate the run has failed.
source: """Shared policy for 37_radius-raid (Radius Raid, twin-stick arena shooter).
One law for every task: kite the swarm, keep the gun pointed at the nearest
threat, and take the crate when the ground is clear enough to go and get it.
The run is a top-down arena shooter on a 1600x1200 field. The ship moves with
WASD (a level-triggered key state, so a direction is held rather than tapped),
its gun fires along `hero.direction`, and that direction is recomputed every
frame from wherever the mouse is: `direction = atan2(mouse.y - hero.y,
mouse.x - hero.x)`. So there are two independent controls and both matter --
movement decides what survives, aim decides what dies.
Three decisions, in this order each step:
* **Fire.** `f` toggles the game's own autofire, which makes the gun fire every
`fireRate` frames in the current aim direction. Arming it once removes the
need to spend a step holding a mouse button, and since one step carries at most
one action, that step is then free for movement or aiming. The probe reports
the live flag, so the press is only made while it is off, with a retry cooldown
so a stale sample cannot toggle it twice.
* **Move.** The eight unit directions are scored by the worst clearance any of
them reaches over a two-second horizon, with the enemies predicted at their
current velocity and the ship's path clamped to the arena. Clearance is a
minimum, not a hard veto: the score stays smooth, so a surrounded ship still
gets a gradient telling it which way out is least bad, and never freezes on a
penalty every option shares. Two things are deliberately in that same minimum:
the enemies over the full horizon (so a direction that ends pinned in a corner
is scored on the enemy closing while the ship cannot retreat), and the arena
edge over a shorter one (so the ship leaves a corner and does not hug the wall,
without the edge dominating the whole decision from the middle of the field). A
continuity term then prefers the heading already held, so an even ring of
enemies does not flip the key state every step.
* **Aim.** The probe returns, per enemy, the lead-corrected intercept and the
page coordinates that point the mouse at it. The policy picks the nearest,
biased toward the one it is already tracking so two equidistant enemies do not
trade the target every step, and spends a step on `mouse_move` only when the
bearing is off by more than a deadband. Movement changes take priority over
aiming, so a needed manoeuvre is never starved; a forced aim every few steps
covers the case where the keys keep being re-snapped while the aim drifts.
Crate greed is the only per-task parameter, chosen in `reset(context)`. Crates
carry health and better weapons, so every task wants them somewhat; the tasks
scored on collecting them want them a lot. The pull fades to nothing as the
nearest enemy closes, because crates drop where enemies die and a greedy ship
walks into the pack to collect them.
from typing import Any, Mapping, Sequence

# Horizon in game ticks (`$.dt` is ~1 per frame, and every velocity in the probe
# is in ticks). The trace at 30 ticks showed why it has to be this long: with a
# half-second lookahead the best-scoring direction was straight into a corner,
# because the chaser was still far and the wall was 180 ticks away, and the ship
# then sat in the corner for nine seconds while the chaser closed and killed it.
# At 120 ticks the same direction's own clearance collapses (the ship reaches the
# corner and has to stop while the enemy keeps closing), so the trap is visible in
# the same minimum that scores the near threat -- no separate veto needed.
# A minimum, so a distant enemy can never outvote a near one; the cap only stops a
# saturated value from being indistinguishable from a merely large one.
# The arena edge enters the same minimum as an enemy would, with this much margin,
# but only over this much shorter lookahead. Scoring the wall as a separate
# additive term does not work -- a path into the wall is clamped, so it predicts
# "the clearance I already have" for the rest of the horizon and a corner becomes a
# stable optimum: the recorded trace has the ship sitting in one for 4.5 s while a
# chaser closed. Scoring it over the enemy's full horizon over-corrects the other
# way: every direction then ends near a wall two seconds out, so the whole score

# Force an aim after this many consecutive movement steps, so a long manoeuvre

# 37_01..37_04 are scored on kills, 37_05..37_07 on crates collected, and
# 37_08/37_09 on seconds survived. Crates help all three (health, faster and
# triple and piercing fire), but only the crate tasks are scored on taking them.
